Apply a pooler to an activation tensor

Source: R/hierarchy_poolers.R
pool_activations.Rd

Reduces a batch of activations to one feature row per image. This is the function extract_feature_hierarchy calls for each stage; you can also call it directly on activations from any backend.

Usage

pool_activations(pooler, a, layout = "nhwc", ...)

Arguments

pooler

An imfeatures_pooler; see poolers.

a

Numeric matrix (N x P) or 4-D array with one image per slice of the first dimension.

layout

Tensor layout for 4-D inputs: "nhwc" (Keras, default) or "nchw" (PyTorch). See as_nhwc.

...

Unused.

Value

An N x P numeric matrix without column names. P is the number of channels times the pooler's columns per channel. Use pooler_feature_names to label the columns.

Details

A 4-D array is first put in N x H x W x C order (see as_nhwc) and then pooled over height and width. A 2-D N x P matrix has no spatial axes and is returned unchanged by every pooler, which is how dense layers pass through a spec.

See also

poolers, pooler_feature_names.

Examples

# PyTorch-style activations: 2 images, 3 channels, 8 x 8 map
nchw <- array(rnorm(2 * 3 * 8 * 8), dim = c(2, 3, 8, 8))
feats <- pool_activations(adaptive_grid_pool(2, 2), nchw, layout = "nchw")
colnames(feats) <- pooler_feature_names(adaptive_grid_pool(2, 2), "layer4", 3)
dim(feats)
#> [1]  2 12
head(colnames(feats))
#> [1] "layer4::channel_001::grid_y1_x1" "layer4::channel_001::grid_y1_x2"
#> [3] "layer4::channel_001::grid_y2_x1" "layer4::channel_001::grid_y2_x2"
#> [5] "layer4::channel_002::grid_y1_x1" "layer4::channel_002::grid_y1_x2"
